monitoring_policy: Internal cost-control governance for this pilot: the project manager may approve reallocations within a single work package up to 5 percent of that package's baseline budget and may commit contingency up to 3 percent of total baseline budget without escalation. Reallocations between work packages, any change exceeding 10 percent of a work package baseline, and any baseline date change affecting a downstream dependency require approval by the Network Infrastructure Steering Group. Resource-hour transfers between work-package pools must be documented as an explicit recommendation and approved by the resource owner before being reflected in reporting. Status reporting occurs at each monthly snapshot using baseline-equivalent effort; variances are reported before any corrective action is proposed, and no scope change may be executed on the basis of a forecast alone.
project_brief: The Northgate Campus Network Modernization project replaces the aging switching, cabling, and wireless infrastructure across three buildings on a single campus. Scope covers a requirements and site survey phase, design of the core and distribution layers, installation of a fiber backbone and structured cabling, deployment of wireless access points and intermediate distribution frame switches, and integration of network monitoring tooling followed by validated cutover. Work is performed by an internal network engineering team supported by contracted cabling crews. The snapshot reflects the reporting point at which approximately the first third of the baseline effort has been consumed, with design work closed out and physical installation underway. Baseline dates, budgets, and effort reflect the approved plan; actual costs and progress reflect records posted through the snapshot date.
